chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen, from Hafs al-Mu'adhdhin, who said:

Ismail ibn Ali led the people in Hajj in the year 140 [AH], so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) fell off his mule. Ismail paused over him, but Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Keep going, for the Imam does not pause.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Ismail ibn Ali, a companion and leader during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling or principle regarding an Imam pausing for personal matters during public duties?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the practical leadership style of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) during the Hajj of 124 AH, where he declined to stop despite falling from his mule, emphasizing that an Imam's duties and presence should not be interrupted by minor personal mishaps. This incident highlights the concept of 'not being detained' (la yaqif), reflecting the Imam's continuous engagement with the community and his status as a guiding authority whose focus remains on the collective religious obligations rather than individual comfort. It serves as a model for leaders to maintain composure and continuity in their roles even amidst personal adversity.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Bin Yaqteen, from Hafs Al Mowzan who said,

‘Ismail Bin Ali led the people to Hajj in the year one hundred and forty, so Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> fell off from his<sup>asws</sup> mule. So Ismail paused over him<sup>asws</sup>, but Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Keep going, for the leader does not pause’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Mansur ibn al-‘Abbas from al-Hassan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from Hafs al-Mu’adhdhin who has said the following: “

Isma‘il ibn Ali (appointed leader for pilgrim) performed al-Hajj in the year 140 Hijriy. Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, fell off his transporting mule and Isma‘il ibn Ali stopped to care for him. Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘Move along with people; the (Imam) leader must not stop.’”
